question: On 11 January 2024, the PSOE and Junts per Catalunya political parties reached an agreement in the Spanish Congress of Deputies to remove from Royal Decree-Law 6/2023 of 19 December 2023 the reform of Article 43a of the Code of Civil Procedure concerning the effect on ongoing proceedings before a Spanish court of submitting a reference for a preliminary ruling to the Court of Justice of the European Union.

In specific terms, a number of political actors said that removing the reform of the new wording of paragraph 2 of this article amounts to a recognition that if a Spanish court submits a reference for a preliminary ruling to the CJEU it will not have the effect of staying the proceedings in relation to which the reference is made.

In this context, in the Commission’s opinion: Under EU law and the Treaties, does the submission of a reference for a preliminary ruling to the Court of Justice of the European Union have a suspensive effect on the proceedings in connection with which the reference is submitted, irrespective of whether this is expressly provided for in national law or not?
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (26.3.2024) Article 23 of the Statute of the Court of Justice of the European Union1 (the Court) determines that in the cases governed by preliminary ruling procedure, the decision of the national court referring a case to the Court suspends the national proceedings.

Accordingly, the Court indicates in point 25 of its Recommendations to national courts in relation to the initiation of preliminary ruling proceedings2 that the lodging of a request for a preliminary ruling calls for the national proceedings to be stayed until the Court has given its ruling.
Moreover, the case-law of the Court has also pointed out that the preliminary ruling procedure requires the proceedings pending before the referring court to be stayed pending the Court’s answer3.

Finally, it follows from the principle of primacy4 that the requirement of EU law to stay the national proceedings until the Court has given its ruling on the preliminary reference applies irrespective of whatever national law would indicate. Therefore, national legislation which would not respect this principle must be disapplied by the national court.
